english.title: Owner / keeper of equine fail to provide ID document on request by vet treating equine
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the

(A)_[owner having primary day-to-day responsibility for an equine, namely **(..SPECIFY EQUINE..), ]_
(B)_[keeper of an equine, namely **(..SPECIFY EQUINE..), for which the owner did not have primary day-to-day responsibility and]_

which was being treated by a veterinary surgeon, namely **(..SPECIFY SURGEON..), failed, upon reasonable request from that surgeon, to provide the equine's ID to

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

without delay
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 11, 24 and 36 of the Equine Identification (England) Regulations 2018.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 37(1) provides that an enforcing authority may impose a civil sanction, or a combination of civil sanctions, under Part 6 against a person if the authority is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the person is guilty of this offence.
(ii) Regulation 37(2) provides that criminal proceedings may not be started or continued against a person if any enforcing authority, in respect of the offence, chooses to apply civil sanctions and services a compliance notice, non-compliance penalty notice or fixed monetary penalty notice on that person.

SUMMARY: A fine
